name: Isabelle
note: generic theorem prover supporting multiple object logics; Isabelle/HOL is its most-used instance
typeSystem: Isabelle is a generic theorem prover built on the higher-order meta-logic Isabelle/Pure and can host multiple object logics. Its most-used instance, Isabelle/HOL, is classical simply typed higher-order logic; theorem construction follows the LCF discipline through a small trusted kernel.
runtime: The Isabelle/ML runtime, built on the Poly/ML implementation of Standard ML, executes the meta-language, the proof kernel, and tactics; Isabelle/jEdit layers an IDE with continuous, asynchronous checking on top.

runtimes.name: Poly/ML
runtimes.role: Standard ML implementation that hosts Isabelle/ML, including the kernel, parser, tactics, and parallel proof infrastructure.

compilers.name: isabelle build
compilers.role: Builds and checks Isabelle sessions, producing cached 'heap images' of verified theories.

concurrencyModel: Independent proof obligations and theories are checked in parallel across CPU cores using Poly/ML's multicore runtime; the underlying logic itself has no concurrency constructs of its own.

codeExample.caption: A simple lemma about natural numbers, proved automatically
codeExample.source:
theory Hello
  imports Main
begin

lemma my_add_comm: "(a::nat) + b = b + a"
  by (rule add.commute)

value "1 + 2 :: nat"

end
